name: White Book on Data Governance and Artificial Intelligence
text_en: Given its recent candidate country status, Moldova  is recommended to step up efforts to mainstream its data -driven development, thereby supporting key economic sectors and strengthening sound governance of data and emerging technologies such as AI.

name: White Book on Data Governance and Artificial Intelligence
text_en: The White Book encourages the alignment of future policy documents on data governance and AI with the EU, OECD and UNESCO guidelines, which should govern the development, design, use, deployment and adoption of AI in various business sectors and across society, to create a principles-level reference framew ork and fundamental requirements that are grounded solidly and comprehensively.

name: White Book on Data Governance and Artificial Intelligence
text_en: The following principles are encouraged that underlie the design, development, use and deployment of AI-based technologies and the adoption of these solutions in society, such as: - Respect for human rights and democratic values; - Human-centered, inclusive, non-discriminatory and unbiased AI; - Diversity, equal opportunities and gender; - Partnership and international cooperation; - Respecting the rights of the child.

name: White Book on Data Governance and Artificial Intelligence
text_en: Human agency: There must be mechanisms to allow human intervention in case the AI system generates unwanted or erroneous decisions.

name: White Book on Data Governance and Artificial Intelligence
text_en: Transparency and explainability: AI systems must be able to explain their decisions and actions in terms that humans can understand.

name: White Book on Data Governance and Artificial Intelligence
text_en: Safety and Security: AI systems must operate in a secure manner and be protected against cyber threats.

name: White Book on Data Governance and Artificial Intelligence
text_en: Adaptability: AI systems should be able to learn and adapt to changes in the environment and feedback received.

name: White Book on Data Governance and Artificial Intelligence
text_en: Accountability: AI developers and operators should be responsible for the correct and ethical operation of their systems.

name: White Book on Data Governance and Artificial Intelligence
text_en: Accessibility: AI should be accessible and useful to all users, regardless of their technical skills or knowledge.

name: White Book on Data Governance and Artificial Intelligence
text_en: Sustainability: AI systems should be developed and operated in a way that respects the principles of sustainable development and has a minimal impact on the environment.

name: White Book on Data Governance and Artificial Intelligence
text_en: Data privacy: AI systems should protect the data they work with, ensuring that personal information is kept safe and used ethically.

name: White Book on Data Governance and Artificial Intelligence
text_en: Interoperability: AI systems should be able to interact and collaborate effectively with other systems and technologies, ensuring seamless integration into various applications and environments.

name: White Book on Data Governance and Artificial Intelligence
text_en: In the context of the EU's ambitions to become a world leader in the field, it is desirable for the Republic of Moldova to align itself with the trends, to create a regulatory framework, to draw a path for the adoption of technologies that are in agreement with the national context and to capitalize on the resources of expertise in sciences, technological innova tion, investments, by involving the academic environment, business, research -innovation, public administration and expertise from the diaspora.

name: Law No. 142/2018 on data exchange and interoperability
text_en: Moreover, Article 11(1) of Law No. 142/2018 on data exchange and interoperability provides that participants holding other states' information systems connect to the interoperability platform on the basis of international treaties. name: Law No. 142/2018 on data exchange and interoperability

name: Law No. 142/2018 on data exchange and interoperability
text_en: In practice, the procedure for cross-border data exchange is regulated by Art. 11 of Law No. 142/2018 on data exchange and interoperability, which provides for cooperation of the competent authority, the National Centre for Personal Data Protection and the participants holding the information systems concerned in the actual data exchange, to ensure all conditions arising from national law for implementing the proposed scenario.

name: Law No. 142/2018 on data exchange and interoperability
text_en: Regarding Action 175 of Annex B to Chapter 24, we note that interoperability of systems, essential for fast, secure and efficient data exchange between authorities, will be achieved on the basis of requests made by the institutions concerned. name: Law No. 142/2018 on data exchange and interoperability
